page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c9a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance designed for CPU-intensive operational workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via a KVM hypervisor, the instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9T25 processor featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs with a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. Dedicated CPU allocation ensures that core compute resources are fully allocated to the workload without contention from neighboring instances.

System memory is configured at 128 GB total, allocating 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage, meaning operating system images and application data rely entirely on external network-attached storage volumes. Network interface capabilities include a baseline network bandwidth of 32 Gbps, supporting efficient multi-node communication and network-based data transfers. No GPU accelerators are provisioned on this instance model.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.c9a.16xlarge delivers qualitative cost efficiency for compute-bound infrastructure that requires high processing power without the overhead of massive memory allocations. The primary tradeoff lies in its dependence on external storage for persistent disk IOPS and the absence of integrated accelerators. This instance profile is optimal for batch processing jobs, software compilation pipelines, CI/CD infrastructure, distributed compute clusters, and high-concurrency web serving.
